title: Ginger Marmalade
subtitle: Seville orange marmalade with a sharp hit of fresh ginger
excerpt: The standard Seville orange marmalade with grated fresh ginger root added at the end of cooking. The ginger heat stays brighter than when cooked from the start. Makes about six 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Ginger added at the end of the boil retains more volatile heat than ginger cooked from the start.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and soak the peel the night before; add ginger only at the final stage.

glossaryTerms.definition: 105 °C for marmalade. Confirmed by the wrinkle test on a chilled plate.

content.text: Ginger marmalade follows the classic Seville orange method exactly, with one addition: freshly grated ginger stirred in at the end of the boil rather than cooked from the start. Cooking ginger dulls its heat into something more mellow; late addition keeps it sharp and bright. Makes about six 450 g jars.

items.prepNote: peeled, finely grated, add at end of boil

content.text: Make the base marmalade using the seville orange recipe. Halve and juice the oranges. Shred the peel and tie the pips and pith in muslin. Simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes until the peel is soft. Squeeze the muslin bundle. Add the sugar, dissolve over low heat, then boil hard to 105 °C (the

When the marmalade reaches 105 °C and passes the wrinkle test, take the pan off the heat and immediately stir in the grated ginger. The residual heat blooms the ginger without cooking it to submission. Skim, rest 10 minutes, stir gently, then ladle into hot sterilised jars and seal.

items.cause: Added too early and cooked out.
items.fix: Always add grated ginger after the pan is off the heat. For more intensity, increase to 100 g.

items.symptom: Ginger flavour is raw and harsh
items.cause: The marmalade was poured too quickly without the off-heat rest.
items.fix: The 10-minute rest allows the ginger to steep in the hot marmalade without further cooking. Don't rush it.

items.cause: Not simmered long enough before the sugar went in.
items.fix: Soft-peel is non-negotiable, press a shred between your fingers before adding sugar.

items.cause: The ginger addition slightly dilutes the set, or muslin wasn't squeezed well.
items.fix: Return to the pan without the ginger, boil to 105 °C again, take off heat, then stir in a fresh batch of grated ginger.
